architecture.heading: How the Architecture Works
architecture.intro: Land replaces VS Code's Electron stack piece by piece. Each element is an independent open-source repository:

mountain.description: Replaces Electron's main process. Manages windows, file system, and process lifecycle at native speed.
mountain.subtitle: Native process manager

cocoon.description: Runs VS Code extensions via Effect-TS. Your existing extensions work without any modifications.
cocoon.subtitle: Extension host, zero rewrites

wind.description: Re-implements the VS Code Workbench. Panels, sidebars, and the activity bar rebuilt without Electron.
wind.subtitle: Full workbench shell

sky.description: Renders the editor interface with Astro. Themes, layouts, and the visual layer load fast on every platform.
sky.subtitle: Themes and layouts layer

air.description: Keeps Land current without interrupting you. Every update is cryptographically signed before it is applied.
air.subtitle: Silent updates, always signed

echo.description: Saturates every CPU core with a work-stealing executor. Heavy indexing stays in the background; the editor stays fast.
echo.subtitle: Uses every CPU core you have

common.description: Shared trait definitions and DTOs used across all elements. The foundation everything else builds on.
common.subtitle: Core shared library

vine.description: gRPC protocol definition bridging Rust and TypeScript at sub-millisecond latency.
vine.subtitle: Native IPC protocol

rest.description: Bundles VS Code platform JavaScript with OXC. Produces the JS runtime Land ships in.
rest.subtitle: Platform JS bundler

output.description: The compiled JavaScript artifacts from Rest, ready for the editor runtime.
output.subtitle: JavaScript runtime bundle

mist.description: WebSocket communication layer between the daemon and the editor frontend.
mist.subtitle: Live WebSocket bridge

grove.description: Hosts native WASM and Rhai extensions alongside the TypeScript extension host.
grove.subtitle: WASM and Rhai extension host

worker.description: Web Workers that offload heavy computation from the main UI thread.
worker.subtitle: Background web workers

sidecar.description: Pre-built Node.js binaries that ship with Land for cross-platform compatibility.
sidecar.subtitle: Bundled Node.js runtime

maintain.description: CI/CD pipelines and maintenance scripts that keep every element building and tested.
maintain.subtitle: Build automation

Nothing is sent anywhere unless you explicitly opt in.
